question: On a marked price of ₹5,000, a dealer offers successive discounts of 10% and 5%. Find the selling price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive discounts can be calculated directly using the multiplying factor method.

Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − D₁)% × (100 − D₂)%

SP = 5000 × 0.90 × 0.95

SP = 4500 × 0.95 = 4275

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹5,000

First Discount (D₁) = 10%

Second Discount (D₂) = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × [(100 − D₁) ÷ 100] × [(100 − D₂) ÷ 100]

 
 

 -10%

 
 

 -5%

 
 
 ₹5,000
 Marked Price

 
 
 ₹4,500
 After 1st Disc.

 
 
 ₹4,275
 Final SP

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 5000 × [(100 − 10) ÷ 100] × [(100 − 5) ÷ 100]

⇒ SP = 5000 × (90 ÷ 100) × (95 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 5000 × 0.90 × 0.95

⇒ SP = 4500 × 0.95

⇒ SP = 4275

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Discount Formula

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the single equivalent overall discount can be found using the formula: D = x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100.

Marked Price (MP)

It is the list price or tag price printed on an article. All discount percentages are calculated on the Marked Price only.

Successive Discounts

When discounts are offered one after another, each successive discount is applied to the newly updated price after subtracting the previous discount, not to the original marked price.
